**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use deferred-state floor in Gate 2 validation**

Gate 2’s validation still hard-requires `≥9 xfailed`, but this same packet now documents an env-driven `XFAIL -> SKIPPED` shift and treats deferred-state as `xfailed + skipped`. With the recorded result (`8 xfailed`, `1 skipped`), this criterion contradicts the packet’s own PASS verdict and can cause strict readers or automation to mark the gate as failed despite the intended deferred-state policy.

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin worktree creation to captured base SHA**

Use the SHA captured in S1 when creating the worktree branch instead of `origin/main`. This command currently rebases on a moving ref, so if `origin/main` advances between S1 and S2 the verification branch can be created from the wrong commit, breaking reproducibility of the series-gate evidence (or forcing a false block on the subsequent HEAD-match validation).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce dirty-check stop condition in preflight commands**

S1 declares a hard stop when the local checkout has tracked changes, but the command list never checks repo cleanliness (no `git status --porcelain`/equivalent assertion), so this packet can proceed from a dirty tree and produce series-gate evidence contaminated by unrelated local edits. That undermines reproducibility for the verification gate because the preflight contract is not actually enforced by the executable steps.

comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce ancestor assertions for prerequisite PRs**

S1 requires PR #709 and #710 merge commits to be ancestors of `origin/main`, but the command list only captures `gh pr view` output and never performs an executable ancestor check (for example via `git merge-base --is-ancestor` on each `mergeCommit`). In scenarios where a PR is merged but not actually contained in the current `origin/main` history, this packet can still proceed and incorrectly mark the series gate as verified.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recompute Gate 1 no-live assertions from repair proof**

comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Assert repair-proof status contract in preflight commands**

S1’s stop conditions and validation require the repair proof to have `status == VERIFIED`, `status_scope == repair_gate_only_not_series_gate`, and `follow_up_packets` containing `TP-RTE-COSTPROFILE-F-VERIFY-002`, but the executable checks only validate the no-live fields. As written, this preflight can pass even if the repair artifact has the wrong scope or does not reference this packet, which undermines the gate’s series-verification dependency check and can certify against an invalid upstream proof.

comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse print-config structure before asserting cost_profile**

Gate 3 claims to verify a **top-level** `cost_profile` field, but the command only runs `grep -q 'cost_profile'` on raw output, which cannot distinguish top-level JSON from any other occurrence in logs or nested data. In runs where `cost_profile` appears elsewhere but the top-level field is missing or malformed, this gate would still pass and could incorrectly mark the series verification as successful.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the unallowlisted .DS_Store artifact**

That file is not in the packet's commit allowlist, while S13 requires every staged path to be allowlisted, so the verification proof can be committed in a state that violates its own governance gate and pollutes the proof tree with a local binary artifact.
